title: Undoing safely: restore, revert and reset

videos.script: Everybody who uses Git long enough types something they regret. {{regret}} The good news is that Git almost never loses anything. The bad news is that there are three commands for going back, their names sound alike, and one of them can hurt other people. {{three}} Restore is for changes you have not committed. You edited a file, it went wrong, you want it back the way it was. {{restore}} Revert is for a commit other people already have. It does not remove anything. It adds a new commit that does the opposite, so everybody's history still agrees. {{revert}} Reset is for commits nobody else has seen yet. It moves your branch back, as if they never happened. {{reset}} That is the rule of this lesson, and the one worth remembering. Revert what is shared. Reset only what is yours. {{rule}} And when reset takes something you wanted, there is a list that remembers where you have been. It is called the reflog, and it has saved more afternoons than any other command. {{title}}
